extracted.intended_audience: system administrators, developers, and users installing/compiling PARI/GP on UNIX-like systems
extracted.subtask_description: Steps, requirements and best-practices for configuring, compiling, testing and installing the PARI/GP library and GP calculator on UNIX systems. Includes optional packages, debugging/profiling builds, testing, documentation and community support pointers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required compiler
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have either an ANSI C or a C++ compiler available to compile PARI/GP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't have one (e.g. /bin/cc on old SunOS), obtain gcc/g++ from the FSF or anonymous ftp. PARI kernel takes advantage of gcc optimizations yielding about 20% speedup on most architectures. You can compile with other compilers but may lose optimizations; note one exception: native AIX C compiler on IBM RS/6000 generates fast code without special help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics support compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The graphic routines in this version have only been tested under X11 and gnuplot, and may not work with old Suntools libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you rely on graphics, prefer X11 and gnuplot; do not assume support for older Sun tools even if nominally supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional packages (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several optional programs/libraries are useful with GP but are not mandatory: GNU readline, gzip/gunzip/gzcat, GNU Emacs, perl, a colour-capable xterm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readline provides line editing, completion and history (preferred readline >= 2.2), but is incompatible with SUN command-tools. gzip enables reading compressed data. Emacs supports running GP inside a buffer; readline still improves completion. Perl provides extended online help. Color xterm enables user-configurable colored output. All are free; get them before proceeding if you want the functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling readline not found
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure may not find readline if it's not installed in a standard place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can compile readline from source in the PARI distribution top-level (no need to install) or create a symbolic link named 'readline' pointing to your readline source directory in the PARI toplevel. Alternatively create readline-osname-arch using PARI's naming convention for Oxxx directories to support multi-architecture builds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic configuration step
rubrics_metrics.description: Run './Configure' in the toplevel directory to configure GP/PARI for your architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use './Configure --prefix=/an/exotic/directory' to install in nonstandard locations (default is /usr/local). Configure creates an Oxxx directory where object files and executables will be built; different architectures produce different Oxxx directories allowing simultaneous builds from same source tree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment variables to override Configure defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure lets AS, CC and DLLD environment variables override defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'env CC=gcc Configure' to force gcc. If using a C++ compiler and you encounter issues with a recent g++, try 'g++ -fpermissive'. Configure may avoid gcc on some architectures; forcing it can be useful to compare benches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive Configure for troubleshooting
rubrics_metrics.description: If default Configure fails, run './Configure -a' (interactive mode) and answer the questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure still provides defaults; do not accept blindly. Look especially for readline and X11 libraries; if missing, follow instructions to provide them (see 'Handling readline not found'). If Configure fails, collect the complete output and the file Oxxx/dft.Config.in for bug reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-architecture build naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure creates Oxxx directories named according to architecture and OS, allowing multiple builds from the same source tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can create 'readline-osname-arch' directories following the same naming convention if needed for per-build readline sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debugging and profiling builds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use configuration flags to build debug or profiling-enabled versions of PARI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run 'Configure -g' to create Oxxx.dbg suitable for debugging (may require tweaking Makefile flags). Run 'Configure -pg' to create Oxxx.prf for profiling (use gprof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation command
rubrics_metrics.description: To compile the GP binary, run 'make gp' in the distribution directory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your make supports parallel builds, change into the Oxxx directory and run 'make -jN' to speed compilation. The default 'make gp' builds probably a dynamic binary (gp-dyn).

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing — basic bench
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the binary with 'make bench' (builds static executable and runs comparative tests) or 'make dobench' to test only default binary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bench should take less than one minute user time on modern machines. Compare static vs dynamic results. If a [BUG] message appears, collect output and include relevant *.dif files in Oxxx and dft.Config.in in bug reports. make bench produces pari.ps (PostScript) in Oxxx for printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing — compatibility and graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional tests: 'make test-compat' for compatibility mode and 'make test-graphic' to test graphics routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic test requires user interaction (click mouse after each image under X11). There will be eight images, possibly shown twice; try resizing windows under X11 to further test. Use 'make test-graphic' only if you have the appropriate graphics environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: [BUG] and error reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If tests show [BUG] messages or other errors, this generally indicates installation issues (or a PARI bug).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send a bug report including complete Configure output, Oxxx/dft.Config.in and relevant *.dif files. Ignore 'not yet available for this architecture' messages unless you implement the functionality yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic library version mismatch handling
rubrics_metrics.description: ld.so may warn that 'libpari.so.xxx has older revision than expected' when an older dynamic PARI library is installed and a broken local configuration exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove the old library or unset LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Unset this variable if anything very wrong occurs with gp-dyn (e.g. Illegal Instruction on startup). This does not affect gp-sta (statically linked).

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation step
rubrics_metrics.description: Install the built artifacts using 'make install' (may require superuser privileges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation writes the default GP executable (likely gp-dyn), libpari (likely libpari.so), include files, manual pages, documentation, help scripts and emacs macros into the directories chosen at Configure time. Beware that installing into the same directory as an older installation may overwrite files from versions <= 1.39.15 but not remove newer-versioned files (which are links to versioned files); periodically delete old pari libraries manually if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Static vs dynamic library installation choices
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, if a dynamic libpari.so can be built, the static libpari.a is not created. You can request static artifacts explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'make install-lib-sta' to install the static library and 'make install-bin-sta' to install a statically linked gp. Static-linked programs may be slightly faster (~5%) but use more disk space, take longer to compile and are harder to upgrade (need recompilation instead of simple library replacement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois package (polgalois) extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Default polgalois computes Galois groups for polynomials of degree <= 7. For degrees up to 10, a separate data archive is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fetch galdata.tgz (likely at the same site as PARI) and untar it into the 'datadir' chosen at Configure time. Then test polgalois with your polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPRC configuration (user defaults)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up $HOME/.gprc by copying misc/gprc.dft (or gprc.dos for GP.EXE) and edit to taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove control characters from the prompt if you lack an ANSI terminal. You can enable colors. Copy/modify misc/gpalias for shortcuts and call it from .gprc. To provide system-wide defaults for all users, copy customized .gprc to /etc/gprc. If gp complains it cannot find gphelp, check .gprc or system-wide gprc for explicit paths and correct them per misc/gprc.dft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing user documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'make doc' produces printable user documentation and requires a working plain TeX installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: make doc creates doc/users.dvi (manual with TOC and index), doc/tutorial.dvi (short tutorial), doc/refcard.dvi and doc/refcard.ps (reference card). Convert .dvi to PostScript using dvips to print.

rubrics_metrics.name: C programming with PARI
rubrics_metrics.description: After installing include files and libraries, you can link C programs to the PARI library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sample Makefile is provided in examples/Makefile to illustrate usage. Run 'make all' in examples to build sample programs (e.g. mattrans.c). Typical Makefile variables: CC, INCDIR, LIBDIR, CFLAGS; link using '-lpari -lm'. Consult examples/matexp.c for a commented example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example GP scripts and explanatory files
rubrics_metrics.description: Several sample GP programs are provided in the examples directory (e.g. SQUFOF, Pollard rho, Lucas-Lehmer and simple class group/unit algorithms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See examples/EXPLAIN for explanations and Section 4.8 for more detail. These are useful for learning usage patterns and for testing your build.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using GP under Emacs
rubrics_metrics.description: GP can be run inside GNU Emacs with provided support files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read emacs/pariemacs.txt for instructions. Even when running under Emacs, using readline is still useful for better automatic completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: PARI community and support channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Three mailing lists (pari-announce, pari-dev, pari-users) are available; most feedback should go to these lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscribe by sending empty messages to pari-announce-subscribe@list.cr.yp.to, pari-users-subscribe@list.cr.yp.to, pari-dev-subscribe@list.cr.yp.to. If you don't want to join the lists, send mail to pari@math.u-bordeaux.fr (they will forward). When emailing as a new user, put 'new user' in the header so maintainers can recognize it. No guarantee of individual replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pentium minor bench discrepancy note
rubrics_metrics.description: Known minor problem on Pentium processors causes slight discrepancies in the last decimals of bench elliptic results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These discrepancies are unrelated to the famous fdiv bug; both results are correct given requested precision. This is informational for interpreting bench results.
